h: Why SENSAS Is Such a Talking Point
p: The concept behind SENSAS started in France, and it's built around a simple idea: we rely on our senses every second of the day without thinking about it, until someone takes one away. Doing everyday tasks without sight, or trying to identify objects using only touch, quickly shows how much we take for granted. It's a lot of laughs, but many people come away surprised at how much they learned about themselves, and about how other people experience the world.

It's a brilliant leveller for groups. The person who's usually loudest might struggle when their eyes are covered, while the quiet one turns out to have a nose like a bloodhound. That's what makes it such a good team-building or birthday activity: everyone gets a moment to shine, and no one can predict who'll be the hero of the day.

Some practical pointers. Arrive a little early so you're not rushing in. Avoid wearing your best clothes, as some challenges get hands-on. Anyone with allergies, mobility needs or sensory sensitivities should mention them when booking, so the team can let you know what to expect and whether adjustments can be made. It's best suited to adults and older children, so check the age guidance if you're bringing younger ones.

Afterwards, why not keep the theme going by treating your senses to some good food? London's food halls, markets and restaurants are never far away, and after two hours of puzzling, everyone will have worked up an appetite. It's also a great way to end the day comparing notes on who got the biggest fright in the dark.
